from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Different light wavelengths rotate at different rates.",
            "White light fans out creating color gradients.",
            "Deeper travel maps a candy-cane helical twist.",
            "Increasing path length makes the twist distinct.",
            "The effect resembles a rotating barber pole."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mechanism: The Barber Pole Effect", lecture_lines)

        # Animation Elements
        # 1. Plane-polarized light vector & Asset
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        barberpole_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/barberpole.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, "E2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(barberpole_asset, "E2", scale_factor=0.4)

        # 2. Sugar solution container & Asset
        container = Rectangle(width=2, height=4, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        sugar_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sugar.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(container, "C4", scale_factor=1)
        self.place_at_grid(sugar_asset, "C4", scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(vector), FadeIn(barberpole_asset))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Indicate color fanning out
        dot_group = VGroup(*[Dot(color=color) for color in [RED, GREEN, BLUE]])
        dot_group.arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_group, "B6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        # Helical path representation
        helix = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([0, t/2, np.sin(t*2)*0.5]),
            t_range=np.array([0, 4]),
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(helix, "D4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(helix), FadeIn(sugar_asset))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6666"))
        self.play(helix.animate.stretch(1.5, dim=1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Rotate vector to represent barber pole effect
        self.play(Rotate(vector, angle=PI/2, about_point=vector.get_start()))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Quantitative Visualization: The Rotation Equation", [
            "Rotation angle depends on concentration and length.",
            "The formula relates angle to physical properties.",
            "Graphs show linear growth of the twist."
        ])
        
        # Load Assets
        cuvette = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cuvette.svg")
        sample = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sample.svg")

        # Define formula: [α] = α / (l * c)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"[\alpha] = ", r"\frac{\alpha}{l \cdot c}",
            font_size=42, color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B3', 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(cuvette, 'A4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(cuvette))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Highlight components
        alpha_part = formula.get_part_by_tex(r"\alpha")
        l_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("l")
        c_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("c")

        self.play(alpha_part.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Highlight l in #00FF00 within cuvette
        self.place_at_grid(cuvette, 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(l_part.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), cuvette.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Highlight c in #00FFFF referencing sample
        self.place_at_grid(sample, 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(c_part.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), FadeIn(sample))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Visual summary
        formula_final = MathTex(
            r"\theta = [\alpha] \cdot c \cdot l",
            font_size=48, color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_final, 'D3', 'D5', scale_factor=1.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_final), cuvette.animate.move_to(self.grid['E3']), sample.animate.move_to(self.grid['E5']))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Saccharimeter", [
            "Saccharimeters measure sugar purity in industry.",
            "They observe rotation to find concentration.",
            "Precision ensures recipes match desired sweetness."
        ])
        
        # --- Visual Elements ---
        # Schematic image
        schematic = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sample.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        # Light source/laser
        laser = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(LEFT*0.5)
        laser_box = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.4, color=WHITE).next_to(laser, LEFT, buff=0)
        
        # Sample cell
        cell = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=2.0, color=WHITE)
        
        # Analyzer/Detector
        analyzer = Rectangle(height=0.6, width=0.3, color=WHITE)
        
        # Polarized light beam
        beam = Line(start=LEFT*1.0, end=RIGHT*1.0, color=WHITE)
        
        # Layout on grid
        self.place_at_grid(schematic, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(laser_box, laser), 'D1', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(cell, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(analyzer, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(schematic), Create(laser_box), Create(laser), Create(cell), Create(analyzer))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Beam passing and rotating
        beam.set_stroke(width=4)
        self.place_in_area(beam, 'D3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(beam))
        self.play(Rotate(beam, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['D3']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        # Adjust analyzer
        self.play(Rotate(analyzer, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['D5']))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Optical Rotation in Sugar Solutions

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Polarized Filter Analogy
sections.content: Define light as an electromagnetic wave oscillating in all directions. Introduce polarizers as 'slotted fences' that restrict light to a single plane of oscillation.
sections.example: Imagine a vertical picket fence allowing only vertical ropes to pass through. If you place a second fence horizontally, no rope gets through (the 'crossed polarizer' effect).

sections.title: The Chirality of Sugar Molecules
sections.content: Introduce the concept of optical activity. Molecules like sucrose are 'chiral'—they have a handedness. When light travels through a chiral solution, the electric field interacts with these molecules, causing the plane of polarization to rotate.
sections.example: Visualize the sugar molecule as a spiral staircase. Light entering the liquid is forced to 'twist' its polarization plane as it interacts with these molecular spirals.

sections.title: Mechanism: The Barber Pole Effect
sections.content: Explain that different colors (wavelengths) of light rotate at different rates. If we use white light, the colors 'fanning out' create a gradient. As we change the concentration or the path length of the liquid, the light 'twists' further, appearing like a rotating barber pole.
sections.example: Use a graphical animation: A beam of white light enters the beaker; as it travels deeper, the polarization vector traces a helix, mapping the 'candy-cane' stripe pattern onto the exit screen.

sections.title: Quantitative Visualization: The Rotation Equation
sections.content: Present the formula θ = [α] × c × l, where θ is the rotation angle. Use a visual graph where θ is the Y-axis and concentration (c) or length (l) is the X-axis, showing a linear growth of the twist.
sections.example: A 'Sugar Meter' device where an animation of a dial moves clockwise as you slide a slider increasing the concentration of sugar in the tank.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Saccharimeter
sections.content: Summarize how this effect is used in the food industry to measure sugar purity. By observing the degree of rotation, we can determine the exact concentration without touching the substance.
sections.example: A quality control robot at a candy factory using a laser and polarized sensors to instantly detect the sugar density in a syrup vat, ensuring the 'sweetness' matches the recipe.
